newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Steady in rangebound trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Steady in rangebound trade.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps were steady as prices remained rangebound in lacklustre trading in the absence of fresh regional news and a relatively steady crude market, traders said.
"It's pretty quiet right now because there's nothing to trade off. The prices are rangebound and people are just waiting for something to happen," one trader said.
September gas oil was last quoted unchanged from Monday at $23.10/$23.20 per barrel with one lots traded at $23.18, brokers said.
It traded several times within a tight 10-cent band on Monday at between $21.10 and $21.20 per barrel, they said.
Traders said market sentiment were unchanged with no incremental buying interest seen from China where stocks remain at a high level and domestic refineries are running at full capacity.

But some are hoping that the shutdown of the bigger 200,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Cilacap's crude unit in October for up to three months will bring in fresh import demand during the start of the fourth quarter at a time when the much awaited winter demand has yet to happen.
Traders estimate gas oil import to reach at least five million barrels and jet fuel at two million barrels.
Cilacap's 100,000-bpd crude unit is currently undergoing a 35-day shutdown beginning August 12.
Already storage tankers in Asia are brimming with middle distillates as the majority of the oil companies are storing their products in the hope of a harsh winter.
The companies are being forced to store their products due to the poor prompt demand and steep contango.
The current poor demand was reflected in the spot physical market where a 200,000-barrel cargo traded at 40 cents below spot Singapore quotes, free-on-board basis.
The cargo was offered at a 30-cent discount in the past week but no buyers emerged.
Singapore fuel oil swaps are steady after physical players emerged on Monday to draw up the trading boundaries. The physical market was bid and offered at between $103 and $105 per tonne.
September fuel oil swaps were last quoted unchanged from Monday at $103.75/$104.50 per tonne and October at $104.25/$105.00, brokers said.
September traded earlier in the day at $104.00 and October at $104.25, they said.
